headline: SILVER SURGES 4%, GOLD-SILVER RATIO BREAKS BACK BELOW 70 — $4,066 Gold and $59 Silver Recover Last Week's Fed-Fear Losses
snippet: Silver surged 4.15% to $59.16 per ounce on July 22 as the gold-silver ratio compressed back below 70:1 — from a high above 70.7 in the prior session when silver had dropped 1.4% while gold held firm — while gold added 1.28% to $4,066.74, recovering the bulk of last week's six-month steepest weekly selloff driven by oil-fuelled inflation fears and rate-hike odds that have since collapsed from 80% to 16.6% for the July 29 FOMC. The compression of the ratio toward 69:1 signals renewed conviction from physical precious metals buyers; historically, ratio readings near 70 at the top of the 50-year range have preceded silver outperformance as the bull market enters its next leg.

headline: DISCOVERY MINING CONFIRMS 4KM GOLD STRIKE AT PAMOUR — 3.05 g/t Au Over 30m; Tony Makuch Eyes Kidd Mill for Higher Throughput (TSX: DSV)
snippet: Discovery Mining Ltd. (TSX: DSV) released results from 47 holes totalling 11,003 metres confirming a large-scale gold deposit at the Pamour Mine in Ontario's Timmins Gold Camp — defining a 4.0-kilometre mineralised strike with highlights including 3.05 g/t Au over 30 metres in the Central Pit, 6.84 g/t Au over 8.5 metres in the North Contact Zone, and 3.14 g/t over 21.2 metres at Pamour West. CEO Tony Makuch — who built Kinross into a multi-million-ounce producer — stated the results confirm Pamour as a large-scale deposit with significant growth potential, backed by the company's acquisition of the Kidd Metallurgical site to increase milling capacity and enable a mine redesign for higher production throughput.

headline: ESKAY MINING DRILLS B.C.'S GOLDEN TRIANGLE — 5,000m Program Opens at C-10; World-Class Structural Geologist Arrives on Site July 22 (TSXV: ESK)
snippet: Eskay Mining Corp. (TSXV: ESK) has mobilised crews and commenced its 5,000-metre 2026 diamond drill program on the Corey-Eskay Property in British Columbia's Golden Triangle, opening at the lower-elevation C-10 prospect due to unusually high snow at primary targets, and targeting chargeability and conductivity anomalies within the Betty Creek Formation that hosts some of the region's highest-grade VMS and porphyry systems. Dr. Brett Davis, an internationally recognised structural geologist, arrived on property July 22 for an eight-day field visit to guide geological mapping and core logging, with a dedicated rapid-turnaround lab now commissioned in Stewart, B.C. to cut assay wait times across the 2026 season.

headline: COPPER JUMPS 3% TO FIVE-WEEK HIGH AT $6.48/LB — China's $100 Import Premium, Chile Storm Hit Codelco; LME Stocks at March Lows
snippet: Copper surged nearly 3% to $6.48 per pound — its highest level in five weeks — as China's premium for imported copper climbed to $100 per tonne (the highest since May 2025) following Beijing's crackdown on VAT fraud that constrained scrap availability and redirected demand to refined copper imports, while a powerful storm system in Chile disrupted operations at Codelco, Antofagasta, and Anglo American requiring safety protocol activations. LME warehouse inventories fell to their lowest level since March as traders redirected metal to China, compressing the global supply cushion at exactly the moment demand signals from the world's largest consumer are turning bullish again.

headline: NdPr ALLOY HITS $133/KG — NEW 2026 HIGH — 21% July Surge Extends Rally; MIIT H2 Mining Quota Decision Is the Next Catalyst
snippet: Neodymium-praseodymium alloy surged 21.4% in July to a new 2026 high of $133.02/kg — clearing the prior March peak near $126/kg — as the market enters its second consecutive year of structural supply deficit driven by EV motor and offshore wind turbine demand growth outpacing mine output, with neodymium metal at $145.88/kg and praseodymium at $149.19/kg now trading above every prior 2026 monthly close. The critical near-term catalyst is China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) announcement of H2 2026 mining quotas, which had not been released as of mid-July; quota tightening would support further gains toward BMI's revised 2026 average forecast of $90,000 per tonne for NdPr oxide, while an expansion would likely cap the current rally.

headline: ENERGY FUELS ACHIEVES FULL-YEAR URANIUM GUIDANCE BY MID-YEAR — Heavy REE Processing of Sm, Eu, Gd, Tb and Dy Commencing at White Mesa (NYSE: UUUU)
snippet: Energy Fuels Inc. (NYSE: UUUU / TSX: EFR) announced it expects to achieve its full-year 2026 uranium production guidance by mid-year — running materially ahead of schedule — while simultaneously commencing modifications at its White Mesa Mill in Utah to enable commercial production of heavy rare earth elements including samarium, europium, gadolinium, terbium, and dysprosium starting in July 2026. The dual milestone positions Energy Fuels as a uranium producer ahead of plan and an emerging heavy REE processor at a moment when uranium spot holds above $85/lb and NdPr has just hit a 2026 high, adding a second revenue stream from a single strategically located mill.

headline: LITHIUM TESTS 4-MONTH LOWS AT CNY 151,000 — Bald Hill and Finniss Restarts Add Supply; ASX Juniors Face Renewed Economics Pressure
snippet: Lithium carbonate prices fell to CNY 151,000 per tonne in July — their lowest level in nearly four months — as Mineral Resources restarted Bald Hill (after an 18-month care-and-maintenance period) and Core Lithium reopened Finniss, adding Australian supply at precisely the moment EV demand concerns resurfaced and renewed sodium-ion battery competition from Chinese producers pressured sentiment. The price retest is forcing a reckoning for ASX-listed lithium developers on project economics; CATL's Jianxiawo mine simultaneously received security clearance to restore activity following its prolonged suspension, adding a further China-side supply signal to an already-pressured spot market.

headline: CHINA'S RARE EARTH INDEX HITS 266: PRICE SIGNAL OR POLICY SMOKE? — MOFCOM Licensing Tightening and Western Supply Gaps Frame the Debate
snippet: Rare Earth Exchanges examines whether China's proprietary Rare Earth Index reaching 266 — a level not seen since the post-COVID supply shock — reflects genuine physical market tightening or a government-managed policy signal designed to pressure Western purchasers ahead of potential MOFCOM export licensing changes, at a moment when the MIIT has delayed H2 2026 mining quota announcements and NdPr alloy has broken to $133/kg. The analysis challenges retail investors to distinguish between real supply deficit dynamics (second consecutive year, EV and wind demand) and short-term price management by Chinese state entities — a critical distinction for junior rare earth explorers who need sustained high prices to attract development capital.
